payload.claim: The pushed commit message asserts flatly that 'the gates were never run to green' whenever `push_unpackaged_work` fires, but the state that triggers it can be `RATE_LIMITED`, and this very spec's own motivating example (`docs/BACKLOG.md` item 45's context) describes 'a rate limit that landed during REBUT, after four commits and green gates' — i.e. a case where the gates *had* run to green before the provider ceiling cut the task off mid-turn (see `saffron/cell/session.py`'s `except RateLimited` branch, which unwinds before `outcome, why = result.state, result.why` is ever reached, discarding whatever the last gate judgement was). The commit message is a persisted, pushed artifact the operator is meant to trust as the record of what happened to unreviewed work, and for this reachable case it tells them something false — that no green gate run ever occurred — which could lead them to discard work that was, in fact, gate-clean. The accurate, always-true claim is 'PACKAGE never ran' / 'this was not verified as ready'; 'the gates were never run to green' is a stronger claim the RATE_LIMITED path cannot actually support.
